channel.title: Said & Checked: New York — AskAmerica
channel.description: What officeholders said each day from or about New York, and which statements government data supports, contradicts or rules out.

item.title: Said & Checked, New York, 2026-11-20: none false or contradicted, 2 unsettled (Dan Goldman)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Dan Goldman, U.S. Representative: “have decimated the cybersecurity personnel that this administration entered office with” Unsettled. OPM headcount data in AskAmerica's warehouse show CISA's workforce fell from 3,379 in January 2025 to 2,197 in September 2026, about 35%, while the FBI as a whole fell from 37,107 to 35,427, about 4.5%. No series isolates FBI cybersecurity staff, so the FBI part cannot be measured, and "decimated" has no fixed threshold.
  • Dan Goldman, U.S. Representative: “The FBI has fired numerous cybersecurity agents because they may or may not have served a subpoena in the Mar-a-Lago case.” Unsettled. As reported by AP, a lawsuit says nine FBI agents, analysts and staff on counterintelligence and counterespionage squads were fired in February 2026 over their roles in the Mar-a-Lago documents investigation, after disclosure that the FBI had subpoenaed toll records. That confirms firings tied to the case, but the suit as reported does not describe them as cybersecurity agents or say the firings were for serving a subpoena; the complaint itself could not be read directly.

item.title: Said & Checked, New York, 2026-11-19: none false or contradicted, 3 unsettled (Chuck Schumer, Mike Lawler)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Chuck Schumer, U.S. Senator from New York: “Reported as: Schumer, the top Democrat in the Senate for nearly a decade, contends that he still has the needed votes to be elected majority leader.” Unsettled. The secret-ballot leadership vote is set for Dec. 1 and no whip count has been published; the AP reports about 15 of the 55 incoming Democratic senators have publicly backed Schumer and four Sen. Chris Van Hollen, which shows neither a majority nor a shortfall.
  • Mike Lawler, U.S. Representative from New York: “in the four major AI platforms, GAO was able to have them create a terrorist manifesto, if you will.” Unsettled. GAO report GAO-27-108814 (Nov. 18, 2026) says covert prompts got all four most-used generative AI platforms to produce feasible plans for mass-casualty attacks and attacks on the electrical grid after first refusing. The report does not use the word "manifesto"; whether attack plans count as the content described is a reading the evidence does not settle.
  • Mike Lawler, U.S. Representative from New York: “they shut the government down for 118 days with respect to the Department of Homeland Security.” Unsettled. As reported by NPR, the House passed the bill ending the DHS shutdown on its 76th day, April 30, 2026, but that bill left out ICE and Customs and Border Protection, whose funding was moved to a separate reconciliation bill whose outcome was not found, so a longer count for part of the department cannot be ruled out. The appropriations record itself could not be read directly.

item.title: Said & Checked, New York, 2026-11-18: none false or contradicted, 3 unsettled (Chuck Schumer)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Chuck Schumer, U.S. Senator from New York: “and I have the votes to continue serving as Democratic Leader” Unsettled. The Dec. 1 Senate Democratic leadership vote is a secret ballot that has not yet been held, and no public count shows a majority of the caucus backing Schumer. Published tallies of declared support (reported as about 14 for Schumer, 4 for Van Hollen and 38 uncommitted) decide nothing either way.
  • Chuck Schumer, U.S. Senator from New York: “Trump arrived in Manila only 30 minutes before the summit ended and is off to China tomorrow to spend the rest of the week with Xi Jinping.” Unsettled. Pre-trip reports from AFP and from ANI (citing the White House) said Trump was due in Manila on the evening of Nov. 17, 'near the summit's conclusion', with a Nov. 18 Marcos visit and then Shenzhen, so the departure for China matches. No report found gives his actual landing time or when the summit closed, so '30 minutes' was neither confirmed nor ruled out.
  • Chuck Schumer, U.S. Senator from New York: “Forget explaining why his administration didn't reveal that a Chinese spy infiltrated one of America's leading companies.” Unsettled. The espionage claim rests on a New York Times report, carried by AP, that U.S. officials concluded the woman involved was a Chinese spy. Nvidia's board says it has no reason to believe secrets were compromised, Singapore authorities found insufficient evidence of a crime, and the FBI and board inquiries are open. No official finding of infiltration or of administration non-disclosure was found.
